node: Precision optical substrates and materials for 800G/1.6T transceivers
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the optical-interconnect substrate/materials node identifies a two-lane universe: reference leaders tied to constrained AI photonics capacity, and underfollowed/speculative suppliers that may benefit if 800G/1.6T optical transceiver qualification cycles and limited commercial-grade substrate supply become binding constraints. Evidence is strongest for Coherent and Lumentum as reference photonics capacity anchors, Fabrinet as a direct manufacturing platform exposed to 800G/1.6T transceiver demand, and Aeluma as a speculative alternative III-V-on-silicon photonics platform. AXT is an important candidate to verify in later passes, but it is not included in the limited list because the provided evidence package does not directly support its current 800G/1.6T qualification or backlog exposure. Layer 1B expands the U.S.-listed universe around the upstream optical-materials chokepoint for AI data-center interconnects. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is AXTI, an InP/GaAs/Ge substrate supplier with explicit data-center InP revenue and backlog evidence. VECO maps to the equipment bottleneck for scaling InP laser production. ALMU is a speculative shadow candidate attempting an alternative InP-on-silicon/III-V-on-silicon scaling route. COHR is included as a high-attention reference anchor because it commercializes 800G/1.6T transceiver and InP-enabled photonics products downstream of the substrate/tooling layer. Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe around the optical-substrate and photonics-materials chokepoint for AI data-center interconnects. T
